text.zh-CN: 缺氧缺血性脑病（HIE）是缺氧和供血不足影响脑功能后的情况，可能出现反应、肌张力、吃奶或抽搐异常；出生窒息与HIE不是同义词。
text.en: Hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE) is disturbed brain function after inadequate oxygen and blood supply, affecting responsiveness, tone, feeding or causing seizures; it is not synonymous with birth asphyxia.

text.en: Preterm babies may also need support because lungs and breathing control are immature; not every breathing problem after birth represents hypoxic brain injury.

text.en: Apnoea, seizures, inability to wake or markedly poor feeding after resuscitation require immediate clinical help; earlier recovery of breathing is not sufficient reassurance.

text.en: Suspected HIE requires early specialist contact when local intensive care is insufficient. The team determines cooling eligibility; families must not use ice packs or cool the baby independently.

text.zh-CN: Apgar记录出生后的心率、呼吸、肌张力等状态，不能单独证明窒息的原因或预测永久损伤；团队还看血气、分娩经过和复苏反应。
text.en: Apgar records heart rate, breathing, tone and other findings after birth; it alone does not establish the cause of asphyxia or predict permanent injury. Blood gases, birth events and response to resuscitation also matter.

text.zh-CN: 脑电图或简化脑电图可发现肉眼不明显的癫痫样放电；MRI帮助判断脑损伤范围。检查时点和临床表现影响解释，一次结果不能代替随访。
text.en: EEG or amplitude-integrated EEG can detect seizures not obvious externally; MRI helps assess the extent of brain injury. Timing and clinical findings affect interpretation, and one result does not replace follow-up.

text.en: The team also checks glucose, electrolytes, kidney and liver function and clotting to assess organs beyond the brain.

text.en: Infection or meningitis, low glucose and other metabolic disorders can also cause reduced responsiveness or seizures; history, glucose and indicated cultures or cerebrospinal fluid tests help distinguish them.

text.en: Brain haemorrhage, structural abnormalities or genetic disease may also cause encephalopathy; persistent or atypical findings need specialist investigation rather than an asphyxia label alone.

text.zh-CN: 急性重症或降温期间由团队决定暂停喂养、少量肠内喂养或静脉营养，不能自行强喂。不同指南在降温期喂养上有差异，应按宝宝状态和当地流程安排。
text.en: During critical illness or cooling, the team determines whether to withhold feeds, use small enteral feeds or provide intravenous nutrition; do not force feeds. Cooling-period feeding differs between guidelines and must follow the baby’s condition and local protocol.

text.zh-CN: 轻度或中度的出生呼吸问题不必然成为HIE；反之，恢复呼吸后仍可出现脑病，需要连续检查，而不是按最初表现一次定论。
text.en: Mild or moderate breathing problems at birth do not necessarily become HIE; encephalopathy can evolve after breathing recovers, requiring repeated assessment rather than a conclusion from the initial appearance.

text.zh-CN: 较早产、轻度HIE、严重出血或重大先天异常者，降温的获益和风险不能从标准中重度HIE研究直接照搬。团队应依据最新证据和具体情况讨论，不能认为越冷越好。
text.en: For more preterm babies, mild HIE, major bleeding or major congenital abnormalities, cooling benefits and risks cannot simply be extrapolated from standard moderate-to-severe HIE trials. The team uses current evidence and individual circumstances; colder is not better.

text.zh-CN: 中重度HIE或接受降温者需多学科发育随访，通常至少覆盖婴幼儿期，并按需要延伸至学龄。即使轻度HIE也应讨论发育评估；出生时轻度窒息但没有HIE者按临床情况安排。
text.en: Moderate-to-severe HIE or cooling requires multidisciplinary developmental follow-up through at least early childhood and longer when indicated. Discuss developmental review even for mild HIE; mild birth asphyxia without HIE follows an individual clinical plan.

text.zh-CN: 急性期可有抽搐、呼吸或循环不稳定、肾功能和凝血异常，需要相应监护和治疗。
text.en: Acute problems include seizures, unstable breathing or circulation, kidney dysfunction and clotting abnormalities, requiring targeted monitoring and treatment.

text.zh-CN: 严重HIE可能留下脑瘫、癫痫、听视力或认知问题；脑瘫指影响运动和姿势的长期障碍，不能从“出生窒息”四个字推断一定发生。
text.en: Severe HIE can leave cerebral palsy, epilepsy, hearing, vision or cognitive problems. Cerebral palsy involves lasting difficulties with movement and posture; a birth-asphyxia diagnosis does not mean it is inevitable.

text.zh-CN: 分娩团队应提前识别风险、准备设备并安排会复苏的人员；突发情况即使产前未预料也要及时处理。
text.en: Birth teams should assess risks, prepare equipment and ensure resuscitation-trained staff are available, including for unexpected emergencies.

text.zh-CN: 稳定宝宝要维持适宜体温并监测呼吸；需要复苏时优先保证有效通气和及时升级照护，不能用保暖或等待自行恢复替代支持呼吸。
text.en: Stable babies need appropriate temperature and breathing observation; when resuscitation is required, effective ventilation and timely escalation take priority over warming alone or waiting for spontaneous recovery.
